Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Utilities Corp. third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Utilities Corp.'s third quarter 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mark Harlan.

Mark Harlan: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational performance in our generation fleet, continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, effective cost management, progress on our infrastructure investments, successful integration of our Evergy Midwest assets, and advancement of our Grid Resiliency Program.

Let me provide some more detail on these six key aspects. First, our generation fleet delivered record volumes of 28.5 TWh, up 12% year-over-year, with standout contributions from our CCGT plants in ERCOT capturing elevated spark spreads and ancillary services. Renewables saw 450 MW commissioned, pushing penetration to 42%, supported by IRA incentives. Cost management through digital twins cut outages 25% and saved $45 million. Infrastructure investments grew our regulated rate base 8% via riders for hardening. The Evergy integration bolstered Midwest wind output at 38% capacity factor. And our Grid Resiliency Program advanced with undergrounding and microgrids to combat storm risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez to discuss the financials.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported earnings per share of $0.98 and revenue of $2.85 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $850 million, primarily focused on renewables and grid hardening. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate raising full-year EBITDA guidance to $4.6-4.8 billion and 2025 EPS to $3.85-4.00, reflecting Q4 tailwinds from winter demand.

To give you more context on our overview of financial performance relative to guidance, we significantly exceeded expectations across key metrics, driven by stronger power prices in PJM and ERCOT, higher renewable dispatch, and disciplined costs amid moderating natural gas prices. Revenues beat our guide by 10% thanks to spark spreads 15% above hedges, generation up 5% with wind at 38% capacity factor, and transmission revenues up 8%. Adjusted EBITDA hit $1.28 billion, 18% above guide, with margins at 45% from 85% hedges. Diluted EPS of $1.52 from continuing ops smashed the midpoint by 17%, aided by O&M 7% under plan. By segment, regulated utilities in line up 10% YoY, renewables 25% ahead with IRA boosts, thermal merchant exceeding by 12%. Northeast data centers, Texas scarcity pricing all contributed, while storage mitigated CAISO curtailments. This validates our Reliable Renewables thesis, with 1.5 GW new clean capacity YTD, nuclear uprates, and CapEx on track at $4.8 billion full-year, 60% to renewables and interconnects. We're raising FY24 EBITDA to $4.85-5.05 billion and EPS to $5.80-6.20.

Building on that, let me walk you through our key achievements and challenges during the quarter, tying them back to our priorities of reliability, decarbonization, and shareholder value. All figures adjusted unless noted. Q3 was standout with adjusted EBITDA at $1.2 billion, up 18% YoY and 5% above guidance midpoint, powered by our 25 GW asset base in a demand-hungry market.

Generation hit record 28.5 TWh up 12% YoY from hyperscale data centers and electrification. In ERCOT, 2.4 GW CCGTs like Liberty Peaker captured $45/MWh spark spreads for $250 million merchant margins, plus 15% more ancillary dispatch. Northeast regulated load grew 4.5%, offsetting milder CDDs with 22% AI commercial demand in PJM.

Renewables commissioned 450 MW: 300 MW SunForge Solar in CAISO with tech PPAs, 150 MW Midwest Wind Harvest in PJM ComEd, hitting 42% portfolio share from 35%, with $180 million IRA PTC/ITC. Solar capacity factors 28% up 3 points from analytics and bifacials; wind 38%.

Efficiency gains: digital twin via GE Vernova Predix cut unplanned outages 25% saving $45 million O&M. Susquehanna nuclear 93% capacity factor with 25 MW uprate. ERCOT BESS 200 MW/800 MWh generated $30 million arbitraging volatility.

Southwest EBITDA up 22%, Northeast rate base $18 billion up 8%, Midwest margins from coal-to-gas retiring 400 MW.

Returned $450 million dividends, $200 million buybacks; CapEx $850 million on AFUDC-rich projects like $1.2 billion Northeast transmission.

Challenges included weather volatility with Southwest heat spiking gas to $3.80/MMBtu costing $60 million unhedged, but 85% hedged at $3.20. CAISO curtailments 5%. Supply chain delayed offshore wind, inflating costs $25 million. FERC Order 2023 stalled 600 MW queue. Rates up debt service $40 million, O&M up 9% to $650 million from labor and nuclear storage. ERCOT negative pricing eroded $15 million.

We're accelerating 1 GW BESS by 2026, prioritizing 12-15% IRR projects, 90% 2025 gas hedges, advocating PJM/MISO reforms. Electrification projects 5-7% EPS growth.

Next, on customer growth and usage trends across residential, commercial, and industrial, which underpin our load outlook. Consolidated customers up 1.8% YoY outpacing U.S. 1.2%, retail sales 4.2% to 28.5 million MWh from electrification, data centers, reshoring.

Residential: 2.1% to 4.2 million customers, usage per up 2.8% to 1,450 kWh. EV 8.5% penetration adding 12% load, heat pumps up 35% post-IRA for 1.2 TWh, hybrid work boosting baseload 4%. Load factor 58%. Southeast strongest at 2.5%.

Commercial: 1.9% to 320,000, sales up 6.1% to 10.2 million MWh led by data centers with 1.2 GW hyperscaler commitments (AWS, Microsoft), usage per large meter +25%, PUE 1.25. Texas 18% commercial load data centers. Retail/office +3%. Volt/VAR shaved 8% peaks. Southeast 7.2%.

Industrial: 0.9% to 12,500, sales +3.7% to 14.1 million MWh from CHIPS/IRA: semis/batteries +12%, green H2 pilots +15%. Usage per +2.9%, load factor 72%. DSM 75% enrollment $25 million credits. Texas +5.1% LNG/frac.

Outlook 4-6% CAGR load growth to 2028 vs. EIA 2.5%. Responding with $1.2 billion transmission, 1 GW VPP, dynamic pricing. Texas 5.5%, Southeast 4.8%. Risks transformers, FERC allocation, but $8 billion 2025 CapEx captures electrification.

Finally, on regulatory lag and mitigation strategies, a key industry challenge where capex outpaces rate recoveries, compressing ROE in high-rate environment at 7.5% WACC. In 2023 $2.8 billion capex up 18% for transmission/renewables yielded 10.5 month average lag costing $185 million or 4% EPS. Peers like Duke 9-11 months.

MISO 8 months via formula post-Elliott; Southeast 12-15 months Vogtle/fuel. Trends worsened 20% from IRA renewables boom to 3.2 GW. Inflation compounds.

Mitigations cap lag under 7 months: trackers/riders recover 95% solar/BESS in 90 days, fuel hedges 70% at $3.20. Formula rates 60% Midwest with quarterly true-ups $120 million avoidance. PBR advocacy in Georgia.

Tech: Palantir AI cuts forecast errors 22% for PJM bids; self-supply peakers/BTM solar; 50 MW VPP $30 million savings. 20% ERCOT merchant lag-free 12% EBITDA. Hyperscaler LOIs bypass regs. FERC advocacy for incentives.

Lag now 2.5% EPS impact vs. 4%, supporting 8-10% 2025 growth.

David Chen: Thank you, Elena. Let me provide an update on the operational front, including our storm response and recovery efforts amid Hurricane Zeta and Midwest polar vortex impacting 40% of 4.2 million customers. Zeta Category 2 near Mobile hit Florida/Georgia with 110 mph winds, 1.15 million outages (28% base); vortex ice snapped 3,200 miles lines, 650,000 outages (22%).

Response: mobilized 4,500 personnel with Duke/Southern/Xcel aid. Skydio drones inspected 1,200 assets +40% damage ID; GE Vernova GridOS AI triaged in 15 minutes.

Restored Southeast 85% in 24 hours, 100% day 5, SAIDI 15% better than 4.2 hour average; Midwest 92% in 48 hours, SAIFI 1.8 vs. SERC 2.5. Beat FPL peers.

Costs $285 million O&M/CapEx ($180M Southeast composites/temp gen; $105M Midwest ACCC), $140 million insurance, recoverable via PSC riders, 2.5% EPS headwind mitigated.

Validates $2.4 billion Grid Resiliency: 1,200 miles undergrounded 70% risk cut, 95% AMI load shedding -20% outages, Tesla microgrids 50 MW 99.9% uptime. Southeast NOAA +15% storms pressure 12% ROE; Midwest ice +18%, wind offset 300 GWh.

Forward: tree-trimming $120 million, DOE $50 million AI grants, 10-15% storm cost cut by 2027, 6-8% EPS growth.

We're also seeing improved efficiency in our CCGT power plants due to the digital twin program, resulting in a 12% increase in output. Our outage rates are down 25%.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery energy storage systems space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the ERCOT market.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed the AI-driven GridOS platform to enhance our defenses against cyber threats.

Mark Harlan: Thank you, Elena, David, Lisa, and Robert. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Thank you. We'll now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Julien Dumoulin-Smith with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Julien Dumoulin-Smith, BofA: Thanks, good morning everyone. Strong quarter on the regulated side, but I wanted to drill into the renewables pipeline. With the IRA PTC and ITC extensions driving such robust development, can you walk us through the updated queue status for your 15 GW solar-plus-storage portfolio? Specifically, how much is interconnection-ready in ERCOT versus PJM, and any updates on PPAs with hyperscalers like Google or Microsoft?

Mark Harlan: Good morning, Julien. Appreciate the question. We're thrilled with the momentum in renewables—our queue now stands at 18.2 GW, up 20% quarter-over-quarter, with 7.5 GW deemed interconnection-ready. Breaking it down regionally: ERCOT remains our growth engine at 4.2 GW ready-to-build, bolstered by recent 1.2 GW PPAs signed with data center anchors—think hyperscalers like the ones you mentioned; we've got term sheets from two majors for 800 MW of behind-the-meter solar tied to their Texas expansions. PJM is a bit stickier with 2.1 GW ready, but we've advanced 1.4 GW through the RTEP process thanks to our grid upgrade contributions. Overall, expect 3-4 GW COD in 2025, with implied yields north of 9% on a levered basis post-ITC. Storage is the real unlock here—our 2-hour lithium-iron-phosphate packs at 60% of projects are yielding 12-15% IRRs standalone.

Operator: Next question from David Arcaro with Morgan Stanley.

David Arcaro, MS: Hi team, congrats on the beat. On the thermal side, natural gas prices spiked 15% YTD—how is that flowing through to your fleet O&M and merchant margins? And with SMRs gaining traction, any color on your NuScale partnership or A-Battery nuclear pilots?

Elena Vasquez: Thanks, David. Gas prices are indeed pressuring the fleet, up 18% MoM in Henry Hub spot, but our hedging covers 85% of 2024 volumes at $3.25/MMBtu fixed, limiting EPS drag to just $0.04. Merchant margins in MISO held resilient at $28/MWh gross, thanks to our 4.5 GW combined-cycle fleet running at 72% capacity factor—outpacing peers like Dominion's 65%. Looking ahead, we're guiding flat thermal EBITDA at $1.2B for FY24.

On nuclear, exciting times. Our NuScale VOYGR SMR MOU has progressed to a 300 MW site control option in our Arizona service territory, targeting FERC licensing by 2026. We've also committed $50M to an A-Battery microreactor pilot with X-energy at our Palo Verde site—synergistic with our 4 GW nuclear baseload, which delivered 92% capacity factor this quarter. This positions us for 10%+ ROE on new nuclear under the ADVANCE Act credits.

Operator: Our next question is from Neal Dingmann with Oppenheimer.

Neal Dingmann, Oppenheimer: Morning all. Capex came in hot at $2.8B this quarter—love the details in the supplement. Can you unpack the AFUDC impact and the rider recovery for your $15B five-year plan, especially with wildfire mitigation in CAISO and grid hardening post-Hurricane Idalia?

Mark Harlan: Neal, spot on. Q3 capex of $2.8B reflects a ramp in transmission—$1.1B deployed, 40% above plan, yielding $180M AFUDC accretion annualized. Our $15B five-year plan is 55% regulated T&D, with full 9.5% ROE recovery via formula rates in our six-state footprint. CAISO wildfire capex is $3.2B through 2027, fully tracked via our Wildfire Mitigation RAMP filing—approved for 100% recovery plus incentives. Post-Idalia, we've accelerated $400M in Southeast resiliency, including 500 miles of undergrounding and advanced reconductoring with ACCC conductors. This de-risks us amid rising extreme weather claims, which were flat QoQ at $120M.

Operator: And from Sophie Karp with Citi.

Sophie Karp, Citi: Thanks. Demand growth has been a tailwind—EVs and data centers adding 2.5% peak load this year. How does that shape your load forecast and rate base growth? Any M&A appetite post your Vistra-like merchant pivot?

Elena Vasquez: Sophie, demand is our brightest spot. Updated 10-year forecast now at 2.8% CAGR through 2033, up from 2.2%, driven by 15 GW data center load commitments—half in PJM, half ERCOT—and EV penetration hitting 25% of light-duty vehicles by 2030 per our EIA-aligned model. Rate base grows to $45B by 2028 at 7% CAGR, all ROE-accretive.

On M&A, disciplined approach: we're eyeing bolt-ons like Talen Energy's Susquehanna nuclear for $1.5B-equivalent, but only at 8x EV/EBITDA with clean FERC transfer. No mega-deals; focus is organic renewables and our $500M share repurchase authorized today.

Operator: Final question from Gregg Orrill with UBS.

Gregg Orrill, UBS: Quick one on guidance. Adjusted EPS $3.85-$4.05 for FY24—any risks from FERC Order 2222 delays or coal retirements? And color on CCUS credits under 45Q?

Mark Harlan: Gregg, guidance intact at $3.95 midpoint. FERC 2222 rollout is lumpy but supportive—our 500 MW battery fleet is DER-aggregated ready in NYISO, targeting $50M ancillary revenue by 2026. Coal retirements: two 600 MW units offline Q4 as planned, offset by 1 GW gas peakers; no margin hit.

45Q is huge—our Petra Nova restart adds $250M NPV from $85/ton credits on 1.6M tonnes CO2 captured annually. Peers like NRG are emulating; we're ahead with DOE grants.

Operator: That concludes today's Q&A. I would like to turn the call back over to Mark Harlan for closing remarks.

Mark Harlan: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Utilities Corp. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Utilities Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
